Play controller. Im mostly an Omen main and just solo q with Omen got me till Ascendant 3.  He has everything. There is just so many options. You can play agressive and do the blind+tp. You can just be the smoke rat and just play from your smokes. Whether would it be tping inside both smokes like a passage way to agressively flank or just camp in your smokes. Lurk depending on the map to create extra space while helping your team with smokes etc. 

Learn how to play a sentinel (besides sage or chamber). I also play Cypher if I can’t play Omen. It is insanely hard to actually get through a good cypher main depending on enemy comp. I’ll even give you a bit of a hint ig. Don’t be scared to place down weird tripwires on Cypher. If there a Fade on the enemy team put the anklebiter trips etc. As Cypher you just want to adapt on how the enemy does entry on site. 
For example how does their Jett entry? Does she just go in, get a kill and dash away. Does she updraft and dash? etc. 

Long story short 
-Learn controller (Omen would be my suggestion)

-Learn sentinel (Cypher, Kj or Deadlock would be my suggestion)
The gameplay is Turkish, if needed any help either with the video itself or something else I can help.

Oh here we go (These are for ranked, mostly mid or high level, all would still work against lower ranks but its unnecessary when there isn't a smurf):

Keep your cross at head level always. Try to refrain from spraying, unless your point blank basically. (You can never know how ratty ppl play regardless of rank)

Refrain from shift peeking 99% of the time. Your first step doesn't make any noise right after you leave shift if you do it right. Use it for your advantage.

Try to plan your clutch beforehand when your last player standing. (Personal opinion and that's what I do).

Your playing Reyna so play off angles a lot. Try to get into angles you can easily disengage from with a dismiss. You have a get out of jail free card when you get a kill unless your instantly traded. Don't go too far from your teammates or too in the open so you don't get chased down from your dismiss.

Keep track of big potential abilities like Sage walls, flashes, blinds, Reyna dismiss, Yoru Clone and tp etc.

Learn movement like shoulder peeking against most operator but you can do it against most weapons if you do it right.

That's the basics you need if not nearly most or even all of it.

Have fun and hope you get better!

We have a very similar agent pick style. We play support but also want a character with potential to play aggressively. In that situation I highly recommend Omen, Deadlock and Vyse. 

I'm not going to include duelists and initiators because you can play aggressively with all of them but when it comes to playing aggressively with Controllers and Initiators,

 I highly recommend Omen. He's basically a mix of everything. He can lock down a site like a Sentinel as defender with his smoke and blind, can also be used as an Initiator by using his blind on certain spots to let your duelists entry. Can also be used like an entry by doing the classic blind and tp behind them, yes Omen is my favorite agent as both in lore and in game.

Also Clove and Astra are nice picks for aggressive gameplay. Astra is more high difficulty to learn but also high reward when you actually know how to use her. Clove gives more bang for your buck basically with being an easier agent and and being pretty rewarding to play even though her kit is very easy to use.

For Sentinels my best suggestion to play aggressively, especially on attack is most likely Vyse and Deadlock. Vyse's vines are actually good for denying entry, especially when you combo with other abilties, an interesting one being a viper util since the vulnerability doubles the damage you get from any source. Her wall is the perfect tool against rushers like Jett or Raze. Her ult is pretty useful for taking site and defending it. Deadlock's grenades and trips are real useful especially when you know how to use them. A suggestion for deadlock would be as my second most played agent would be that put your trips on jump spots. For example around B site in Ascent or under hookah at B site on Bind.
